name: @stackguardian/backstage-plugin-sg-library
readme:
# Overview

Welcome to the sg-library plugin!

This plugin can be used to deploy stacks and workflows using templates present on SG platform directly from backstage app.

# Compatibility

- Backstage `1.57` or later (legacy frontend system, `@backstage/core-plugin-api`)
- React 17 or 18

# Installation & Usage

1. Add the plugin to your Backstage frontend package:

```bash
# Yarn 4 (Backstage default)
yarn workspace app add @stackguardian/backstage-plugin-sg-library

# Yarn 1
yarn --cwd packages/app add @stackguardian/backstage-plugin-sg-library
```

2. Configure the StackGuardian organization and the backend proxy in `app-config.yaml`:

```yaml
integrations:
  stackguardian:
    organization: ${SG_ORG} # StackGuardian organization name

proxy:
  endpoints:
    '/stackguardian':
      target: https://api.app.stackguardian.io/api/v1
      headers:
        Authorization: apikey ${SG_API_KEY}
      allowedHeaders:
        - x-sg-orgid
      changeOrigin: true
```

**Regions:** set `target` to your organization's region. The plugin links to the matching dashboard automatically:

| Region | `target`                                     | Dashboard                           |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| EU     | `https://api.app.stackguardian.io/api/v1`    | `https://app.stackguardian.io/`     |
| US     | `https://api.us.stackguardian.io/api/v1`     | `https://us.stackguardian.io/`      |

For other API hosts, set `integrations.stackguardian.dashboardUrl`. The plugin's config schema exposes only the proxy `target` URL to the frontend. Headers such as the API key stay on the backend.

Set `SG_ORG` and `SG_API_KEY` in the backend's environment. See the [StackGuardian docs](https://docs.stackguardian.io/docs/api/overview/#steps-to-generate-an-api-key) to create an API key.

The plugin calls StackGuardian through the Backstage proxy (`@backstage/plugin-proxy-backend`), so the API key stays on the server and the browser doesn't hit CORS errors.

3. Mount `SgLibraryPage`, either as a page route in `packages/app/src/App.tsx`:

```tsx
import { SgLibraryPage } from '@stackguardian/backstage-plugin-sg-library';

<Route path="/sg-library" element={<SgLibraryPage />} />;
```

or as an entity tab in `packages/app/src/components/catalog/EntityPage.tsx`:

```tsx
<EntityLayout.Route path="/sg-library" title="SG Templates">
  <SgLibraryPage />
</EntityLayout.Route>
```

Template cards have a copy-link button. The copied URL (`?templateId=...&templateType=...`) opens the deployment form for that template directly.
